// c1stw: stop-the-world under load. Four workers spin in call-free loops (a flag check every 65536 iterations)
// while main forces eight collections; the runtime must stop the spinning workers for each GC. The workers run
// until main has finished collecting, so every collection happens under load.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"runtime"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
)

func main() {
	const workers = 4
	runtime.GOMAXPROCS(workers)
	var stop atomic.Bool
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	sums := make([]uint64, workers)
	for w := 0; w < workers; w++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func(w int) {
			defer wg.Done()
			h := uint64(w + 1)
			for i := 0; ; i++ {
				h = h*6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
				if i&0xffff == 0 && stop.Load() {
					break
				}
			}
			sums[w] = h
		}(w)
	}
	before := new(runtime.MemStats)
	runtime.ReadMemStats(before)
	const k = 8
	for i := 0; i < k; i++ {
		runtime.GC()
	}
	after := new(runtime.MemStats)
	runtime.ReadMemStats(after)
	stop.Store(true)
	wg.Wait()
	var d uint64
	for _, s := range sums {
		d = d*1099511628211 ^ s
	}
	fmt.Printf("gc forced %d, at least %d collections: %v\n", k, k, after.NumGC-before.NumGC >= k)
	_ = d
	fmt.Println("workers", workers, "done")
}
